title: fix(subagents): keep owned runs in activity counts
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Long-running subagents can disappear from activity counts and stop blocking another spawn or parent settlement even while their current execution owner or exact queued reservation remains active. Recent ownerless routing records can also be reported as live executors.

## User Impact

Subagent lists, status counts, spawn-capacity checks and unfrozen parent settlement retain work that this process can prove is still owned. Saved routing metadata alone no longer proves an executor is running. Quiet workers were already preserved by the sweepers; this patch does not claim to fix workers being killed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing live-context and exact collector-reservation predicates for retained accounting, and correlate compact read projections with the matching raw generation without granting those projections mutation authority. Recent unowned rows retain the existing bounded grace period. Terminal and suspended-delivery rules remain unchanged.

This is separate from #122849's ACP lifecycle ownership and #126924's wait-expiry classification. Both exact-head overlaps were assessed and the narrow shared-file boundary posted on those PRs. No ACP task, spawn, stop, cleanup, wait-result or persistence implementation is added here. No existing contributor patch is replaced.

## Evidence

- Original real-owner baseline: three accounting failures and three controls passed. Quiet-current-owner sweeper controls already pass on baseline.
- Repaired owner, list and reservation-projection coverage passed. Serial recovery completed the previously missing registry checks: 166 registry plus 26 archive tests, 192 total. The interrupted run and stale-lock failure remain failures, not relabeled passes.
- Integrated onto `a941bb47519c24d71bf60dc11ec862e6444b4721` at `11cef54278f0e05061fae56fa52af217846a717e`, with all 14 candidate files byte-identical to the final reviewed freeze. Current-base actual-owner and Gateway session-list suites passed 9 and 34 tests, 43 total.
- Current-base required changed-code checks passed (exit 0): `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base a941bb47519c24d71bf60dc11ec862e6444b4721`. Core/test typechecks, three zero-entry dead-export scans, changed-file lint, state/database guards and zero runtime import cycles passed. Canonical live-owner, scheduler, generation and scope dependencies are byte-identical across the old and integrated bases.

Independent P0-P2 review returned a P1 cross-process concern, not a clean verdict. The same no-local-owner age fallback exists on the baseline, so the finding does not establish an introduced regression. The documentation now limits owner retention to facts the reading process can verify. Cross-process liveness remains unproved and is not repaired by a speculative lease or schema. A proposed cross-agent bare-child-key collision also lacks a supported producer and is not claimed fixed.

No native Codex, remote-worker or physical-restart proof is claimed by this local accounting patch. No schema, stored codec, lease, public configuration, retention or permission change.


## CI fixture correction

Signed head `762c171045bf58c73e228abf633b2591f2eb79a8` adds only three test/support corrections after the production head reviewed above. Hosted CI exposed a shared registry mock missing the canonical `hasLiveAgentRunContext` export and two older positive fixtures that registered metadata without an execution claim. The mock now represents no owner; positive fixtures acquire/release actual claims and retain a metadata-only negative.

All four affected files passed: **35 Gateway + 66 registry tests = 101 tests**. The targeted three-file changed check passed, and fresh independent P0–P2 review found no actionable issues in this delta. Production and documentation bytes are unchanged. The original cross-process P1 finding and documented disagreement remain intact; a clean fixture review is not a blanket clean-review claim. New-head hosted CI is pending.
